correctness.rationale: For each arrival the centered root-depth average is a square-integrable martingale. Conditional parent-copy coupling gives cross-increment covariance alpha times the cross-sectional depth covariance. The centered-sample update proves both finite recurrences and a directly checked product solution. The identical-tree variance dominates the two-tree process, bounding L2 martingale increments by O(log n/n^2). A nonnegative generating-function integral and exact partial fractions evaluate the absolutely convergent covariance series. Endpoint limits and strict convexity follow by domination and strictly positive zeta coefficients. The separate check.py enumerates all paired histories through six vertices for five rational couplings, verifies 273 exact/numerical checks; this supports, but does not substitute for, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Copying parent decisions introduces microscopic dependence of a fixed strength, and total root path length is a canonical global growth/search-cost statistic. Determining exactly how local copying propagates into the macroscopic rooted path cost is a motivated structural question. The complete nonlinear covariance transfer C(alpha), strict attenuation rho(alpha)<alpha, zeta-series interaction coefficients and finite exact recurrences are not merely normalization or a known endpoint. The theorem gives a quantitatively usable second-order model characterization while explicitly excluding inaccessible-root inference claims.
